questions.prompt: A 100 Ω and a 500 Ω resistor are in **series** across 24 V DC. How much current flows, in milliamps?
questions.explanation: In series the resistances add: 100 Ω + 500 Ω = 600 Ω. I = 24 V / 600 Ω = 0.04 A = 40 mA.

questions.prompt: Four pilot lights are wired in **parallel** across a 24 V DC supply. Each draws 30 mA. How much current does the supply provide, in milliamps?
questions.explanation: In parallel each branch draws its own current, and the currents add: 4 × 30 mA = 120 mA.

questions.prompt: Which of these are true of parts wired in **parallel**? Choose every one that is.
options: Each part has the full supply voltage across it
The same current flows through every part
If one part opens, the others keep working
The total resistance is the sum of the parts
questions.explanation: Parallel branches share the voltage, not the current: each gets the full supply, and each has its own path, so one opening leaves the rest working. Same current and resistances adding are true of series.

questions.prompt: Two switches, A and B, are wired in **series** with a lamp. Fill in when the lamp is lit (TRUE = closed, or lit).
questions.explanation: In series there is one path: the lamp is lit only when A and B are both closed.
